scope: Four illustrative measured-derived Small IN100 grain-surface, point-cloud, numeric interchange, and point-to-grid pipelines; occurrences are not independent filter verification. Stages 03 and 04 use complementary tiles and do not claim duplicate-removal coverage.

filters.purpose: Read the measured-derived, unsmoothed ROI24 mesh; original positive FeatureIds and both FaceLabels components are preserved.
Expose original FaceLabels component 0; keep the two-component source array intact.
Expose original FaceLabels component 1; keep the two-component source array intact.
Mark faces where neither original label equals 2205; true means remove, and either label slot can establish ownership.
Keep all faces touching grain 2205, compact vertices, and carry original ownership arrays without stale normals or network NodeTypes.
Copy selected vertices and triangles into a calibrated micrometer Triangle Geometry; extraction does not propagate the unit.
Copy the original two-sided FaceLabels and scalar components to the calibrated geometry.
Name copied source labels OriginalFaceLabels; they record ownership and are not used as local orientation labels.
Drop the temporary uncalibrated selected mesh.
Assign connected surface components in a local namespace; region 1 must contain the complete 508-face shell.
Repair inconsistent triangle winding using the single local surface RegionIds, then orient the closed shell outward.
Recompute per-face area on the repaired shell in square micrometers.
Compute unit normals from the final outward-oriented triangle winding.
Keep the cropped source image for context but omit the full multi-grain mesh from the selected-grain checkpoint.

Export the repaired compact grain shell as zero-based numbered node and triangle tables. Coordinates use micrometer numbers rounded to four decimal places. These space-delimited files omit units, ownership arrays and solver definitions; retain the native checkpoint.
Save the complete original-identity grain shell as the measurement-stage checkpoint.
Read the verified complete-grain checkpoint; this stage does not rerun extraction.
Allocate a two-component int32 face array for local exterior and grain labels.
Fill all tuples with the stated local labels.
Create two local measurement rows: unused exterior 0 and occupied grain region 1.
Allocate original reconstructed FeatureId lookup for the local rows.
Map local row 1 to original reconstructed FeatureId 2205; row 0 is unused.
Integrate the repaired, closed shell using local [-1,1] face labels; row 1 is the enclosed cubic-micrometer volume.
Average unique surface vertices for local grain 1; this is a vertex mean rather than a volume centroid.
Give every face sampling-local labels [0,1]: outside the selected shell and original grain 2205. Keep the [-1,1] surface-measurement labels and original neighbor labels unchanged.

Sample the closed shell at the existing source image cell centers, preserving its exact origin, spacing and units. MeshSampledGrainIds 1 should match original FeatureIds 2205; zero means outside this selected grain, not necessarily void.

Summarize local grain 1 from nominal-grid membership: count, count times voxel volume, and equivalent sphere diameter. Exclude background row 0; a changed count under perturbation is a sampling effect, not physical grain growth.

Average equal-volume cell centers from recovered local grain 1. This is a volume centroid for the voxel reconstruction, distinct from SurfaceVertexMeans. It uses the same local row 1 -> original 2205 mapping.

Use fixed seed 2205 and bounded 0.05 micrometer perturbations on the source grid. X is drawn per point, Y once per row, Z once per slice; this is an illustrative correlated positioning scenario. Labels remain stored at nominal grid locations.

Reconstruct the same calibrated image grid with a correctly designated Cell Data matrix. Issue 1800 misassociates the uncertain sampler output; this 24-cubed fixture also avoids its non-cubic tuple-order defect.
Copy the sampled labels unchanged onto the correctly associated nominal grid. This does not move or resample the values.
Remove only the temporary misassociated image after its sampled labels and calibration are retained.
Create local rows 0 and 1 for the sampling result; only row 1 represents the selected original grain 2205.

Summarize local grain 1 from nominal-grid membership: count, count times voxel volume, and equivalent sphere diameter. Exclude background row 0; a changed count under perturbation is a sampling effect, not physical grain growth.
Mark nominal cells whose sampled membership changed: absolute difference of local 0/1 labels is 0 for agreement and 1 for a change.

Use fixed seed 2205 and bounded 0.2 micrometer perturbations on the source grid. X is drawn per point, Y once per row, Z once per slice; this is an illustrative correlated positioning scenario. Labels remain stored at nominal grid locations.

Reconstruct the same calibrated image grid with a correctly designated Cell Data matrix. Issue 1800 misassociates the uncertain sampler output; this 24-cubed fixture also avoids its non-cubic tuple-order defect.
Copy the sampled labels unchanged onto the correctly associated nominal grid. This does not move or resample the values.
Remove only the temporary misassociated image after its sampled labels and calibration are retained.
Create local rows 0 and 1 for the sampling result; only row 1 represents the selected original grain 2205.

Summarize local grain 1 from nominal-grid membership: count, count times voxel volume, and equivalent sphere diameter. Exclude background row 0; a changed count under perturbation is a sampling effect, not physical grain growth.
Mark nominal cells whose sampled membership changed: absolute difference of local 0/1 labels is 0 for agreement and 1 for a change.
Export local row IDs, original FeatureId mapping, enclosed volume, and surface vertex mean for inspection.
Save the calibrated shell with original identity, local labels, and audited measurements.

filters.pipeline: (03) Small IN100 Grain Point Cloud Registration.d3dpipeline
filters.purpose: Save source context, complementary calibrated tiles, the reassembled cloud, all three moving checkpoints, and the known and ICP residual transforms.
Read four numeric datasets from TileA: 89 XYZ tuples and matching scalar metadata. Declare tuple/component shapes explicitly; no transpose, geometry, units, or NX structure is imported.
Read four numeric datasets from TileB: 81 XYZ tuples and matching scalar metadata. Declare tuple/component shapes explicitly; no transpose, geometry, units, or NX structure is imported.
Append TileA then TileB rows for Coordinates_um: 89 + 81 = 170 tuples. Use the same order for coordinates and every scalar; preserve the input numeric type and component shape.
Append TileA then TileB rows for SourceROICellIndex: 89 + 81 = 170 tuples. Use the same order for coordinates and every scalar; preserve the input numeric type and component shape.
Append TileA then TileB rows for FeatureIds: 89 + 81 = 170 tuples. Use the same order for coordinates and every scalar; preserve the input numeric type and component shape.
Append TileA then TileB rows for Image Quality: 89 + 81 = 170 tuples. Use the same order for coordinates and every scalar; preserve the input numeric type and component shape.
Split all three XYZ coordinate components into scalar columns while retaining Coordinates_um as an inspection checkpoint.
Combine X_um, Y_um, Z_um columns in that exact order into 170 three-component vertices. Keep physical coordinates unchanged: normalization and source removal are disabled.
Move six scalar columns into ReassembledCloud/Vertex Data so each row describes the corresponding vertex. Leave imported tiles and both assembled coordinate arrays as inspection checkpoints.
Export all point tuples, including valid row zero, in an explicit six-column CSV with headers.

Record each source point's containing cell and fail on any out-of-bounds point. GridCellIndex is an ownership/inspection result; Interpolate Point Cloud v4 independently computes its own indices from coordinates.

Average ImageQuality64 only within each containing cell: Uniform kernel size 0.25 micrometers is below 0.5 micrometer spacing, so the integer radius is zero. Contribution counts distinguish observed cells from zero-filled empty cells.

Spread ImageQuality64 into a 3 by 3 by 3 grid-cell neighborhood using Gaussian sigma 1 in each axis (one cell offset, or 0.5 micrometers here). Kernel weights use integer cell offsets, not exact point-to-center distances. Positive counts outside observed cells are estimates, not new measurements.
